summary.headline: G R Infraprojects Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 64% YoY to INR2,019 crores, but standalone EBITDA margin slipped to 9.49% on war-driven input costs.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was about INR2,019 crores, up roughly 64% YoY from INR1,234 crores, while consolidated revenue rose about 45% to INR2,325 crores. Standalone EBITDA margin was 9.49% versus 9.76% a year ago, with management attributing 2-2.5% of cost pressure to oil-linked price escalation in construction inputs. Order book stood at about INR24,577 crores as of 1 October 2026, with a further INR19,346 crores of bids awaiting opening. Working capital days rose to 152 from 128 at FY26-end, driven by HAM debtors and inventory.

segments.name: Oil and gas (offshore/pipeline EPC)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 turnover about INR900 crores; FY27 full-year turnover guided around INR1,200 crores. Order backlog about INR300 crores; target to win about INR2,000 crores of new orders this year, with about INR1,000 crores revenue in FY28. Receivables about INR720-740 crores.

segments.name: Agra-Gwalior DBFOT toll (HAM/BOT)
segments.commentary: Order value about INR3,686 crores; appointed date received and included in order book. Revenue guidance about INR250 crores in FY27 and INR1,200-1,400 crores in FY28.

segments.name: HAM monetisation
segments.commentary: Five to six completed HAM projects planned for monetisation this year, with about INR1,250 crores equity invested. InvIT distributions guided at INR13-14 crores for the full year; Q2 distribution was INR3.55 per unit including INR1.17 capital repayment.

segments.name: Power transmission
segments.commentary: Pipeline about INR92,000 crores; focusing on about INR32,000 crores. Bids for about INR1,000 crores submitted and awaiting opening; targeting additional projects of INR3,500-4,000 crores. NTPC battery project under force majeure and renegotiation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now expected near 20% (earlier about 15%); about INR5,000 crores revenue expected in H2 FY27.
FY28 growth targeted around 15%, subject to order inflows; execution capability cited up to 20%.
FY27 order inflow target maintained at about INR20,000 crores; management says it is attainable if bidding is fair.
Standalone EBITDA margin targeted around 10-11%; likely 11% if input costs stabilise, otherwise around 10%.
Capex: about INR83 crores in H1 FY27, with INR150 crores more guided for H2; total INR200-250 crores for FY27, and about INR200 crores in FY28.
Promoter equity infusion of about INR3,100 crores pending on HAM/BOT projects: about INR500 crores in FY27 and about INR2,500 crores in FY28 (per management).
capex_capacity: Capex H1 FY27 about INR83 crores; guided INR200-250 crores for FY27 and around INR200 crores for FY28.
Net block of PPE including CWIP and intangibles about INR1,015 crores at end Sep 2026; Q2 fixed asset additions INR60 crores.
Investments in subsidiaries (loans and equity) about INR2,687 crores at end Sep 2026.
Agra-Gwalior appointed date received; two other projects worth INR3,562 crores still awaiting appointed dates, expected by end-December or January.
BharatNet project slowed by right-of-way issues; clearance expected around January with pickup from Q4.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR24,577 crores as of 1 October 2026, versus INR26,400 crores on 1 April 2026 and about INR25,000 crores at June-end; management said the movement reflects scope changes, escalation and maintenance additions net of execution.
Order inflow target of INR20,000 crores for FY27 split roughly INR13,500 crores transport, INR2,500-3,000 crores tunnels, INR3,500 crores power transmission, and INR500-600 crores ropeways/other.
Management said NHAI pipeline is promising but few projects awarded in H1; net-worth criterion (20% of unexecuted portfolio value) under new HAM disqualifies weaker bidders.
Input cost inflation from oil-linked products: bitumen cost largely compensated by the authority, but petroleum-linked costs in transport, cement and steel absorbed, worth about 1.5-2% of margin.
PSP (pumped storage) orders targeted around INR3,000 crores each; qualification varies by project, with one bid qualified via JV and another directly.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the order book movement small versus revenue booked, and how will H2 growth look?
qa_highlights.answer: Net order book movement reflects scope, escalation and maintenance additions; H2 revenue expected about INR5,000 crores, implying FY27 growth near 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR20,000 crore inflow target realistic given competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the INR20,000 crore target, citing projects of INR3,000-5,000 crores and bids submitted; said it is achievable if government bidding is conducted properly.

qa_highlights.question: Is the NTPC battery project cancelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said force majeure was invoked due to war-driven battery price spikes; NTPC has issued a revised bid with extended timeline and terms are under discussion, not formally cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin decline and is cost pass-through complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin impact of about 2-2.5% from war-linked construction cost increases; bitumen compensated, but other petroleum-linked costs (1.5-2%) absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the working capital increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise mainly to inventory build in power transmission, and to HAM debtors that SPVs pay as and when required; oil and gas receivables take about 90-100 days.

qa_highlights.question: What are the HAM monetisation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Five to six completed HAM projects with about INR1,250 crores equity invested planned for monetisation this year, targeted by December or January, all in cash.

risks_watch: Order inflow lag versus peers; INR20,000 crore FY27 target depends on award timing, with few H1 awards so far.
Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 18.63% from 24.16%; monitor its drivers and the cost pass-through gap.
Working capital days up to 152 from 128; HAM debtors INR1,490 crores and oil and gas receivables around INR720-740 crores due around March.
Consolidated D/E rose to 0.60x; promoter equity commitment of about INR3,100 crores over FY27-FY28 requires funding.
NTPC battery project status and terms pending; BharatNet execution slowed by right-of-way issues.
Oil and gas turnover expected to decline from about INR1,200 crores in FY27 to about INR1,000 crores in FY28 due to seasonality.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and the long-term pipeline, but cautious on order inflows, awards timing and cost pressure. Management raised FY27 growth guidance but kept margin guidance at 10-11% and was non-committal on the NTPC project.
key_quotes: Considering the growth which we have witnessed in H1 of this fiscal, we are expecting that the growth would be closer to 20%.
From an execution perspective, we are fully confident that we can comfortably achieve up to 20%; however, there are still some challenges regarding order inflow.
The main reason remains around 2% to 2.5% impact due to the increase in cost of construction, which is driven by due to this war impact and price escalation on oil related products.

growth.why: Management raised FY27 standalone revenue growth to ~20% (from ~15%) and expects ~INR5,000 cr revenue in H2 FY27, backed by an INR24,577 cr order book and the Agra-Gwalior HAM project (appointed date received), though the INR20,000 cr order inflow target depends on fair bidding and few NHAI awards so far in H1.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets 10-11% standalone EBITDA margin (11% only if input costs stabilise, otherwise about 10%) versus 9.49% in Q2 FY27, so expansion depends on oil-linked cost relief; consolidated margin fell to 18.63% from 24.16%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Agra-Gwalior DBFOT (order value INR3,686 cr) has its appointed date and is guided at INR250 cr FY27 and INR1,200-1,400 cr FY28 revenue, while two more projects worth INR3,562 cr await appointed dates by end-December or January; BharatNet slowed by right-of-way issues with clearance expected around January.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone revenue grew 64% YoY to INR2,019 cr in Q2 FY27, H2 FY27 revenue is expected at about INR5,000 cr, and FY28 growth is targeted around 15% (execution capability up to 20%) backed by a INR24,577 cr order book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex guided at INR200-250 cr for FY27 and about INR200 cr for FY28, with no utilisation figure given, and the spend is mainly HAM/BOT equity rather than new plant, so no new capex programme is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 standalone revenue growth was raised to near 20% from about 15%, with about INR5,000 cr expected in H2 FY27, but margin guidance was held and order inflow is uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin was 9.49% against the 10-11% target, with 2-2.5% war-linked cost pressure and 1.5-2% of petroleum costs absorbed; the INR20,000 cr order inflow target depends on awards, and only INR24,577 cr order book is held with few H1 awards; NTPC battery project is under force majeure and renegotiation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Power transmission bids of about INR1,000 cr are awaiting opening, PSP orders of about INR3,000 cr each are targeted, and oil and gas aims to win about INR2,000 cr of new orders this year with about INR1,000 cr revenue in FY28; these are new order wins rather than product launches, and the brief names no new products.

rows.label: HAM monetisation via InvIT (5-6 projects, ~INR1,250 cr equity)
rows.why: Management plans to monetise five to six completed HAM projects this year, all in cash, with InvIT distributions guided at INR13-14 cr for the full year and Q2 distribution at INR3.55 per unit including INR1.17 capital repayment.

rows.label: Working capital days reversal
rows.why: Working capital days rose to 152 from 128 at FY26-end, with HAM debtors of INR1,490 cr and oil and gas receivables of about INR720-740 cr due around March; the timing of SPV payments and inventory build in power transmission will decide the reversal.

rows.label: Promoter equity infusion for HAM/BOT projects
rows.why: Promoter equity infusion of about INR500 cr in the rest of FY27 and about INR2,500 cr in FY28 is planned, against consolidated D/E already at 0.60x and borrowings of INR5,938 cr.

tone.note: Management was confident on execution, the HAM pipeline and raising FY27 growth to about 20%, but cautious on order inflow timing, the NTPC battery project status and 2-2.5% war-linked cost pressure.
